rv.q: Now for the bad news about Thea Sharrock’s production.

To be able to get through the shear number of power ballads and upbeat tracks each night is nothing short of astounding and she deserves every round of applause and standing ovation that gets thrown at her after performances of "I Have Nothing" and "I Will Always Love You."
This spectacle of a show is definitely worth another visit.
For all the cheesiness – there is plenty, including a 60 foot projection of Richards that Knight serenades during the finale

cn.t: Beverley Knight's powerhouse vocals electrify this cinematic musical adaptation, though the production relies heavily on Whitney Houston's iconic songbook to carry a familiar story that doesn't fully transcend its film origins.
